comparison.objective: Set a telescoping gauge to a bore diameter and leave it retained on a stand, versus set a gripper opening stop and lock it.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-1880 uses bore contact, gauge rocking, plunger locking, extraction, and placement; the candidate uses coaxial driver/wrench seating and countertorque against jam-nut reaction.
comparison.success_condition: Both retain a calibrated setting after release, but PR-1880 requires a span within 0.10 mm and stand placement, while the candidate requires nut seating and repeated gripper actuation with limited drift.
comparison.reason: Setting retention is shared, but contact metrology and withdrawing a telescoping gauge test a different physical ability from locking an adjustment screw under coupled torque.
